title: Lesson 69: CTA Design Scenario Practice: A Real Scenario End to End
description: Taking the whole architect toolkit and pointing it at one messy client scenario: how to read a requirement, fix the system of record, design the data, integration, identity, and security models as one coherent whole, write measurable targets, record the tradeoffs you accepted, and turn it all into a board-grade presentation you can defend.

questions.question: Per the lesson "CTA Design Scenario Practice: A Real Scenario End to End", what is the correct first step a candidate should take when attacking a design scenario?
options: Extract the why and restate the requirements in your own words before touching a diagram.
Immediately draw the object model on the whiteboard.
Choose the integration pattern before reading the full scenario.
Write the non-functional requirements before identifying the system of record.
questions.explanation: Step 1 of the method is to read for the why and restate the requirements before any diagram. If you solution the literal sentences, you build whatever the client described instead of whatever the business needs.

questions.question: In the Aurora Manufacturing Group walkthrough, why does the order-placement integration use a queue that the ERP polls in batches rather than a synchronous call on every order save?
options: Because the lesson says synchronous calls are always an anti-pattern.
Because the ERP's SOAP API degrades badly under load, so the queue lets the ERP consume work at its own pace and protects the highest-volume operation.
Because Salesforce cannot send data to external systems in any other way.
Because the budget prohibits synchronous integration entirely.
questions.explanation: The ERP's SOAP API is reliable on small payloads but degrades under load. The highest-volume order-placement operation goes through a queue the ERP polls in batches, so the ERP consumes at its own pace, and every handler is idempotent so a retried delivery cannot create a duplicate fulfillment.

questions.question: Which statement best reflects the lesson's guidance on setting non-functional requirements in a design scenario?
options: NFRs should be left as general quality wishes the client can interpret.
NFRs must be measurable targets, such as a four-second pricing target at 1,500 concurrent users, chosen to match the client's actual landscape.
NFRs are only about the Salesforce platform's own availability and never about recovery targets.
NFRs should be deferred until after the solution is built.
questions.explanation: NFRs with no numbers are not requirements. In the walkthrough the targets are measurable, such as pricing in under four seconds at a peak of 1,500 concurrent users, and every number is chosen to match the landscape, quarterly peaks, business-hours users, and an ERP that cannot take real-time load.
